key_insight: An evolutionary, model-guided process can automatically grow a proof-assistant interface that is better optimized for AI agents than human-designed tools.
engineering_relevance: For theorem-proving systems, the interface itself becomes a tunable component that can reduce solve cost and latency while improving success rates across different models.
method: Start with a baseline prover interface and let a frontier model propose new interface features.
Keep only features that improve end-to-end performance of smaller agent models on curated math problems.
Deploy the evolved server as an MCP interface for Rocq, then port the same design to Lean.
evidence_signal: On the held-out miniF2F-Rocq test split, the evolved Rocq MCP server outperformed both a compiler-only baseline and an established MCP server across four models from two families in success rate, cost per solve, and time per solve; it also improved cost and time on a subset of PutnamBench when transferred to Lean.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated on curated benchmarks and a transferred subset, so real-world gains may depend on problem distribution and careful integration with each prover’s tooling.
paper_title: Growing an Agent/Prover Interface: Evolutionary Tool Design for Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving in Rocq and Lean
